speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass; to determine the cause, how old are you and when did these symptoms begin? Additionally, have you experienced any pain, weight loss, or changes in bowel or bladder habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the adnexal mass, I need to clarify the characteristics of the mass and rule out systemic causes. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, CA-125, and FSH/LH. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: NORMAL READINGS; Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: NORMAL READINGS; CA-125: NORMAL READINGS; FSH/LH: NORMAL READINGS; Pelvic_Ultrasound: Thickened endometrial stripe and left adnexal mass observed

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound shows a thickened endometrial stripe and a left adnexal mass, but your CA-125 and hormone levels are normal. To better characterize the adnexal mass and rule out malignancy, I need to see more detail. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_MRI_with_contrast. Do you have a history of taking hormone replacement therapy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Hyperplasia (likely secondary to an estrogen-secreting ovarian cyst or tumor causing the adnexal mass). The thickened endometrial stripe in a postmenopausal woman is highly suspicious, and the normal CA-125 makes advanced ovarian cancer less likely, pointing towards a functional cause like a cyst or a low-grade tumor producing estrogen.
